comments.body:
## RE-TRIAGED under the refined bar (accurate-fit-to-scenario-set) → now READY-TO-FIX

Original tag was `escalate` on the premise of a cross-surface vocabulary decision. Under the refined standard, an existing broad-accurate code suffices, so no escalation is needed for the minimal correct fix.

**Why the current code is MISLEADING:** the hardcoded `error="llm_unavailable"` names "the provider is down" for the entire `except rebar.llm.LLMError` scenario set of the 4 gate tools — which includes input rejections (LLMInputRejectedError), self-inflicted stops (RunawayToolLoopError, LLMBudgetExhaustedError), oversized input (ContextWindowExceededError), and output defects (StructuredOutputError/UnretryableOutputError/CompletionRecoveryError). The code contradicts most of its scenario set.

**Recommended fix — narrow, using existing vocab:** derive the `error` field instead of hardcoding — `llm_unavailable` **only** when `isinstance(exc, LLMUnavailableError)` (whose scenario set — extra absent, bad credentials, provider unreachable/rate-limited — accurately fits the name), otherwise `command_failed` (broad-accurate: "an unclassified rebar failure"). The dict already carries the truthful `resolution_class`/`retryable`/`diagnostic` from `outcome_of(exc)`, so a client keeps the fine disposition; only the misleading top-level `error` string is corrected. No new vocabulary → ready-to-fix.

Enriching `error` with a per-disposition code finer than `command_failed` stays OPTIONAL/deferred (pursue only on demonstrated consumer need).

## Finding (audit of epic 3405-c0b7)
**Site:** `_structured_llm_failure(exc)` in `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:22` — returns `{"error": "llm_unavailable", ...}` with the string hardcoded, regardless of the `LLMError` subclass. Called by all four MCP gate tools (`review_code`, `scan_spec`, `verify_completion`, `review_plan`) in their `except rebar.llm.LLMError` arms.

**Exception types mis-labeled:** the non-availability `LLMError` subclasses that can reach these arms — `LLMInputRejectedError` (docstring: "must never surface as 'the LLM provider call failed'"), `RunawayToolLoopError` (same explicit contract), `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` (rebar stopping itself), `ContextWindowExceededError` (input too big), `StructuredOutputError` / `UnretryableOutputError` / `CompletionRecoveryError` (output defects). All get top-level `error="llm_unavailable"`.

**Wrong code:** `llm_unavailable`.
**Mitigation already present:** the same dict carries `resolution_class` / `retryable` / `diagnostic` from `outcome_of(exc)`, so a client that reads `resolution_class` gets the truthful disposition (e.g. CHANGE_INPUT, FIX_AGENT_DESIGN). But an agent that branches on the top-level `error` field is actively misled.

**Observable vs latent:** OBSERVABLE — live MCP surface, returned to the driving agent.

**Proposed fix (needs decision):** derive the top-level `error` field from the exception subclass / `resolution_class` instead of hardcoding (e.g. input-rejection → an input code, output defect → an output code, genuine outage → `llm_unavailable`). This needs a code-vocabulary decision consistent with `error_code_for` and the `coverage.llm_unavailable` flag → **escalate** (cross-surface consistency + likely new vocabulary). Behavior-change to a producer.

**caused_by / class:** second, independent site of the blanket `LLMError -> llm_unavailable` pattern (origin 8a31).
